speaker: Bhairava (dhāraṇā 68)
question: How is eternal brahman touched?
premises: Of letter with emission: emission-ending awareness make.
By supportless mind: may touch brahman eternal.
inference: Supportless awareness on the emission-ending letter touches eternal brahman.

speaker: Bhairava (dhāraṇā 69)
question: What is meditated on?
premises: Sky-formed own self meditated, by directions uncovered.
Supportless awareness power: own form will show then.
inference: Meditating sky-formed self uncovered by directions, own form shows.

speaker: Bhairava (dhāraṇā 70)
question: What is pierced?
premises: Something limb pierced first with sharp needle etc.
Right there awareness yoked: in Bhairava spotless going.
inference: The pierced limb yokes awareness — spotless going in Bhairava.

speaker: Bhairava (dhāraṇā 71)
question: What is inside me?
premises: Mind-etc inner-making not is inside me: think thus.
By absence of fancies: fancies abandoned may be.
inference: Denying inner-making, fancies fall away by their absence.

speaker: Bhairava (dhāraṇā 72)
question: What is māyā?
premises: Māyā deluding: named, of part counting standing.
Counting the natures of realities: not separately may be.
inference: Māyā is delusion's name — counted realities never stand separately.

speaker: Bhairava (dhāraṇā 73)
question: What dissolves sudden desire?
premises: Sudden desire arisen, having seen: to calm should lead.
Where arisen, thence right there dissolves.
inference: Seen desire led to calm dissolves where it arose.

speaker: Bhairava (dhāraṇā 74)
question: Who am I without desire?
premises: When desire unarisen, knowing or why: then I am indeed.
Truly He-I: thus become, in that dissolved, that-minded may be.
inference: Unrisen desire reveals He-I — dissolved, that-minded.

speaker: Bhairava (dhāraṇā 75)
question: What is seen in desire or knowing?
premises: In desire or in knowing arisen: mind should set.
Self-mind undivided: then reality-meaning seeing.
inference: Setting mind undivided in either, seeing of reality's meaning follows.

speaker: Bhairava (dhāraṇā 76)
question: What is causeless knowing?
premises: Causeless may be, supportless, error-natured: truly not this of anyone.
Thus becoming Śiva, O dear.
inference: Knowledge not anyone's own becomes Śiva — denial turns identity.

speaker: Bhairava (dhāraṇā 77)
question: What distinguishes bodies?
premises: Consciousness-natured: in all bodies distinction not is anywhere.
Made of that all contemplating: world-conquering person.
inference: No bodily distinction: contemplating all made of consciousness, one conquers the world.
